entry.title: Track your complaint
entry.description: Enter the Complaint ID you were given when you reported. We'll send a verification code to the mobile number on file before showing any case details.
entry.stagesPreviewTitle: What you'll see once you're verified
entry.heroImageAlt: A magnifying glass resting beside a laptop on a marble surface.

case.heading: Complaint {publicId}
case.notFoundBody: Check for a typo, or look in the SMS we sent you.
case.noContactTitle: We can't verify this one online
case.noContactBody: This complaint has no mobile number on file, so we can't send a verification code for it. Contact your State/UT Grievance Officer with your Complaint ID.
case.verifyDescription: We'll send a code to the mobile number on file for this complaint. Two things together, this ID and that code, are what let you see the details.
case.mockedOtpTitle: Prototype: OTP is mocked, not a real SMS
case.mockedOtpBody: Sent (mocked) to {maskedMobile}. Demo code: {code}. See <link>what's real vs mocked</link>.
case.genericError: That code didn't match. Try again.
case.noStatusYet: No status updates yet. Check back soon, this page will show each step as it happens.

gaps.transactionRef: The transaction ID or UTR, without it the bank cannot locate the payment, so a hold cannot be requested.
gaps.suspect: Anything about who did it, a UPI ID, an account number, a phone number or a link. The account the money went to is what a bank can actually act on.
gaps.evidence: A screenshot or recording. Not required, but it is what turns a statement into evidence.

case.completeBody: Nothing is needed from you right now. You can still add information at any time if something changes.

matchedOn.pincode: Matched to this unit by your PIN code.
matchedOn.district: Matched by district, no unit covers your exact PIN code in this prototype.
matchedOn.state: Matched by state only, so this is the closest unit rather than the exact one.

case.officeCaveat: This is an invented unit for the prototype, not a real police station, and nothing you filed here was sent to it. To reach a real one, call 1930.
case.noOfficeMatched: We could not match your PIN code to a unit. Call 1930, they will route you to the right cyber cell.
case.whoDidItTitle: What you told us about who did it
case.additionsDescription: Your original report is never changed. Anything you add appears here, in order.
case.documentsDescription: Paperwork the officer has filed. You can print or save any of these.
case.viewFir: View and print the FIR copy

RECEIVED.label: Reported
RECEIVED.meaning: We have your complaint and it's in the system.
RECEIVED.whatYouCanDo: Save your Complaint ID if you haven't already. No action needed yet.

SENT_TO_BANK.label: Sent to your bank
SENT_TO_BANK.meaning: The transaction details were forwarded so the bank can attempt to freeze the funds.
SENT_TO_BANK.whatYouCanDo: Call your bank's fraud helpline directly too. Don't rely on this alone.

WITH_CYBER_CELL.label: With Cyber Cell
WITH_CYBER_CELL.meaning: Your case has been assigned to a police cyber cell for review.
WITH_CYBER_CELL.whatYouCanDo: No action needed. This can take time, and that's normal.

UNDER_INVESTIGATION.label: Under investigation
UNDER_INVESTIGATION.meaning: An investigating officer is actively working your case.
UNDER_INVESTIGATION.whatYouCanDo: Keep any new evidence (screenshots, messages). You can add it to this case.

EVIDENCE_REQUESTED.label: Additional evidence requested
EVIDENCE_REQUESTED.meaning: The investigating officer needs more information or evidence from you to move this case forward.
EVIDENCE_REQUESTED.whatYouCanDo: Reply through the contact on file, or add what you can when you're contacted. Don't share OTPs, passwords, or card PINs with anyone, even someone claiming to be the investigating officer.

DISPOSED.label: Handed to a police unit for investigation
DISPOSED.meaning: This does not mean your case is closed. "Disposed" is police-internal wording for "assigned onward": it is not a rejection and it is not the end.
DISPOSED.whatYouCanDo: Keep following up with your bank. If weeks pass with no update, use the grievance officer contact for your state.

FIR_REGISTERED.label: FIR registered
FIR_REGISTERED.meaning: A First Information Report has been formally registered for your case.
FIR_REGISTERED.whatYouCanDo: The investigating officer's contact should follow. Keep your FIR number safe.

WITHDRAWN.label: Withdrawn
WITHDRAWN.meaning: This complaint was withdrawn and is no longer active.
WITHDRAWN.whatYouCanDo: If this wasn't you, contact the grievance officer for your state immediately.

add.title: Add information to your report
add.description: Report {publicId}. Anything you add is attached to it and is visible to whoever handles the case.
add.appendOnlyTitle: Your original report will not change
add.appendOnlyBody: What you first wrote stays exactly as it is, that is what makes it usable as a statement. Anything you write here is added underneath it, with the date.
add.label: What would you like to add?
add.placeholder: For example: they called me again from a new number, or I found the transaction reference on my bank statement.
add.help: There is no minimum length. Write it however it comes.
add.doneBody: It now appears under your original report, with today's date.

errors.NOT_VERIFIED: Your access to this report has expired. Open it again from /track and verify with the code.

It is not an official NCRP acknowledgement, this report number is not a real NCRP complaint number, and nothing in it was filed with cybercrime.gov.in, any bank, or any police unit. To file a real complaint, use cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.
